open_points.subject: A19-1 Required test 5
open_points.text: the link's origin, path and other parameters unchanged
open_points.question: Must inserting the stored query value also preserve the link's fragment, including the absence of a fragment?
options: Preserve the existing fragment exactly, including keeping no fragment when none existed.
Require links under this test to have no fragment, and keep them fragment-free.
Leave the fragment unconstrained even though origin, path and query parameters are preserved.

witness.initial: An owner-page link has origin https://registry.example, path /project, query parameter view=card, and fragment #details; the stored value for parameter label is x#summary.
events: The renderer places the stored value in the label query parameter.
The owner follows or inspects the rendered link.
outcomes: The link is https://registry.example/project?view=card&label=x%23summary#details; label reads back as x#summary and the original fragment remains.
The label still reads back as x#summary and origin, path and view remain unchanged, but the renderer clears or replaces #details because the test never constrains the fragment.
witness.observer: The owner, whose navigation lands at a different fragment.

open_points.subject: A19-1 Required test 5
open_points.text: the link's origin, path and other parameters unchanged
open_points.question: Does “unchanged” require the serialized URL components and parameter ordering to remain byte-for-byte identical, or only the same parsed origin, path and other parameter names and values?
options: Require semantic equality after URL parsing; harmless encoding normalization or parameter reordering is allowed.
Require byte-for-byte preservation of every unaffected serialized component and the ordering of query parameters.
open_points.default_guess: Require semantic equality after parsing while preserving every unaffected name and decoded value.

witness.initial: A link contains other=a%20b before the renderer inserts the stored query value.
events: The renderer uses a URL builder that normalizes the existing parameter to other=a+b while adding the new value.
A test or owner inspects the resulting href.
outcomes: The result passes because other still parses as the same value a b.
The result fails because the serialized spelling of the other parameter changed.
witness.observer: The factory check and an owner inspecting or copying the href.
